outcome_evidence: The panel finds the principal claimant is a Convention refugee and accepts her claim (though her US-citizen minor son's claim is rejected).
basis_evidence: She alleged sexual assault by bandits targeting her over her father's activism and was found to face persecution as a member of the particular social group of women fearing gender-related violence in Haiti, with no SOGIE element.

timing_evidence: The claimants fled Nigeria to the USA in 2018 and 'travelled to Canada on [XXX] 2019; where they filed for protection,' with no prior entry to Canada indicated, so the claim was filed upon first entry.
outcome_evidence: The panel finds the principal claimant (along with the associate adult and minor male claimants) to be Convention refugees and accepts their claims.
basis_evidence: The principal claimant alleged persecution by Nigerian society and state authorities because of her bisexuality (SOGIE), with the family members' fears derivative of her sexual orientation.

timing_evidence: After the Afghan government collapsed on August 15, 2021, the claimants (previously living in the US) 'chose to travel to Canada XXXX XXXX, 2021, and submit claims,' which were deferred only until later in 2021, so the claim was made within a year of first entry.
outcome_evidence: The panel finds the principal claimant, associate claimant, and minor male claimant are Convention refugees and accepts their claims (only the US-citizen minor female's claim is rejected).
basis_evidence: Alongside the principal claimant's political-opinion fear of the Taliban, the claimants alleged that 'the female claimants will face gender-based persecution and harm from the Taliban due to their membership in a particular social group as females,' with no SOGIE element.

timing_evidence: The principal claimant came to Canada in XXXX 2019 and formally converted in XXXX 2020, but the decision never states when the refugee claim was made, so the gap from first entry cannot be computed.
outcome_evidence: The panel finds both claimants are Convention refugees under section 96 and accepts their claims.
basis_evidence: The claimants alleged persecution in Iran based on religion — the principal claimant's conversion to Christianity and the associate claimant's apostasy/renunciation of Islam — not gender-based or SOGIE persecution.

timing_evidence: The decision describes events in China through the forced abortion in [XXX] 2018 but gives no date of the claimant's arrival in Canada or of the making of the claim, so the gap cannot be determined.
outcome_evidence: The panel finds the claimant is a Convention refugee as a woman who violated the family planning policy and accepts her claim.
basis_evidence: She alleged gender-specific persecution — forced IUD insertion, forced abortion, a fine, and threatened sterilization under China's family planning policy, as a member of the particular social group of women who violated the policy — with no SOGIE element.

timing_evidence: The decision recounts time in the United States (including a baby born there in November 2017) and travel to Canada on their passports, but gives no date of first entry to Canada or of making the claim, so the gap cannot be determined.
outcome_evidence: The member accepts the claims of the principal, associate, and minor claimants, finding them Convention refugees based on the principal claimant's bisexuality.
basis_evidence: The principal claimant alleged persecution in Nigeria as a bisexual woman at the hands of police and the community (SOGIE), with the family members' fears derivative of her sexual orientation.

timing_evidence: The claimants 'fled to Canada on temporary residence visas in July 2018 and initiated these inland refugee protection claims a few weeks after their arrival,' with no prior entry to Canada indicated.
outcome_evidence: The member concludes the claimants are Convention refugees and accepts their claims based on perceived anti-government political opinion.
basis_evidence: The principal claimant alleged persecution arising from a business dispute with a well-connected landlord, an accusation of insulting the Iranian regime, and anti-regime political activity in Canada — political persecution, not gender-based or SOGIE.

timing_evidence: The claimant came to Canada on a visa to attend a conference scheduled for XXXX 2022 and the member notes 'this claim was made in December of 2022, shortly after your arrival,' with no prior entry to Canada indicated.
outcome_evidence: The member concludes the claimant is a Convention refugee on account of his Tigrayan ethnicity and professional profile and accepts the claim.
basis_evidence: He alleged detention, torture, and threats by Ethiopian police and by Qeerroo/Fano groups due to his Tigrayan ethnicity, perceived support of Tigray forces, and outspokenness against the government — ethnic/political persecution, not gender-based or SOGIE.

timing_evidence: The claimant was stopped in transit in London before ever reaching Canada, flew to Chicago in 2018, and four days later first entered Canada at an irregular crossing at Emerson, Manitoba where he started his refugee claim the same day.
outcome_evidence: The panel found the claimant is a Convention refugee pursuant to section 96 of IRPA and accepted his claim.
basis_evidence: The claim was based on imputed political opinion arising from Al-Shabaab's attempted forced recruitment of the claimant and its perception of him as a westernized returnee and possible spy.

timing_evidence: The decision gives no date of arrival in Canada and no date the claim was filed, so the gap between first entry and the claim cannot be determined.
outcome_evidence: The panel concluded the claimants are Convention refugees because of their Coptic Christian identities and accepted their claims.
basis_evidence: The family alleged intimidation, harassment and assault by Muslim extremists because of their religious identity as Coptic Christians in Egypt.

timing_evidence: The principal claimant left Colombia for Canada in 2021 and filed an inland refugee protection claim later in 2021, a gap of well under one year with no indication of any earlier entry.
outcome_evidence: The panel found the principal claimant and her family to be Convention refugees within the meaning of section 96 and accepted the claims.
basis_evidence: The principal claimant alleged persecution by FARC dissidents (Dagoberto Ramos Mobile Column) on account of imputed political opinion due to her work as a social activist and human rights defender.

timing_evidence: The principal claimant entered Canada in 2018 after the fall 2018 police incident and filed her claim shortly after arriving, a delay the panel described as approximately a month or two.
outcome_evidence: The panel found the principal claimant and her children to be Convention refugees and accepted their claims.
basis_evidence: The principal claimant alleged years of domestic abuse by her former partner in Barbados and claimed as a member of the particular social group of women fearing domestic violence.

timing_evidence: The decision recounts the claimant's 2020 detention in Rwanda but gives no date of arrival in Canada and no date the claim was made, so the gap from first entry cannot be determined.
outcome_evidence: The panel found the claimant to be a Convention refugee pursuant to section 96 and accepted the claim.
basis_evidence: The claimant alleged imprisonment and risk to his life from the Rwandan authorities based on imputed political opinion arising from his father's membership in the FDU opposition party.

timing_evidence: The claimant came to Canada in 2022 after learning that year that Mexicans could travel visa-free and made his refugee claim in August 2022, a gap of less than one year.
outcome_evidence: The panel found the claimant is a Convention refugee with respect to both Venezuela and Mexico and accepted his claim.
basis_evidence: The claimant alleged threats and attacks by a corrupt Venezuelan politician and his associates after making police complaints exposing corruption, grounded in imputed anti-government political opinion.

timing_evidence: The decision refers only to photos posted during her travels to Canada and gives no arrival date or claim date from which the gap could be computed.
outcome_evidence: The panel found the claimant is a Convention refugee facing a serious possibility of persecution for religion and imputed political opinion, and accepted her claim.
basis_evidence: The claimant alleged she would be punished as a non-believer for un-Islamic behaviour including posting photos without the hijab or chador required for women in Iran, a gender-specific dress code, with the Gender Guidelines applied.

timing_evidence: The claimant first came to Canada as a student in 2015 and remained on student visas, filing for refugee protection in late 2020, more than five years after first entry.
outcome_evidence: The panel accepted the claim, finding the claimant a Convention refugee under section 96 due to a serious possibility of persecution in Morocco.
basis_evidence: The claimant, a 24-year-old lesbian, alleged persecution in Morocco on account of her sexual orientation, including criminalization of same-sex relations.

timing_evidence: The principal claimant arrived in Canada in 2023, learned two weeks later that security officers were seeking her, and the claimants then applied for protection, with the decision rendered December 21, 2023, so well under one year after her first entry.
outcome_evidence: The panel determined the three claimants are Convention refugees under section 96 and accepted their claims.
basis_evidence: Alongside the political-opinion allegations from treating injured protesters, the principal claimant alleged rape threats from a suspected Basij member and she and the minor claimant alleged persecution on a gender basis as females in Iran.

timing_evidence: The decision does not state when the claimant first entered Canada or when she filed her claim, so the gap cannot be determined.
outcome_evidence: The panel found the claimant is a Convention refugee as a lesbian woman in Uganda and accepted her claim.
basis_evidence: The claimant alleged persecution as a lesbian (criminalized same-sex activity, community and police targeting) as well as gender-based harms including forced marriage to an older man and sexual assault by a police officer in detention, with Guidelines 4 and 9 both applied.

name: Tegene v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a judicial review of an RPD decision dated October 12, 2017 determining that the applicant was not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicant left Ethiopia for Canada later in 2012 and claimed asylum, with no indication of any earlier entry to Canada or delay in claiming.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was granted and the RPD decision set aside, with the matter remitted to a differently-constituted panel.
basis_evidence: The claimant alleged persecution by the Ethiopian government for her political activities on behalf of the Unity for Democracy and Justice Party, including two detentions and a beating.

name: Abdelgadir v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a judicial review of a RAD decision dismissing the applicant's appeal and confirming the RPD's rejection of his refugee protection claim.
timing_evidence: In February 2017 the applicant went to Canada and filed his refugee protection claim, with no indication of any earlier entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed, upholding the RAD's negative credibility findings.
basis_evidence: The claimant alleged detention and torture by Sudanese authorities because of his participation in anti-government protests and perceived political opposition.

name: Djubok v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a judicial review of an RPD decision rejecting the applicants' refugee protection claim on state protection grounds.
timing_evidence: Ms. Djubok and her family came to Canada in 2011 and the family then claimed refugee protection, with no indication of any earlier entry or delay.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was allowed and the matter remitted to a differently constituted panel for re-determination.
basis_evidence: The principal claimant alleged risk as a female Roma victim of some fifteen years of serious domestic violence (with additional Roma ethnicity and disability-based risks for her son), and no SOGIE allegations.

name: Otero Chapital v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a judicial review of a December 1, 2004 RPD decision that the applicant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no dates for the applicant's entry to Canada or for when she made her refugee claim.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed.
basis_evidence: The Uruguayan claimant alleged a well-founded fear of persecution based on her perceived political opinion and a risk of cruel and unusual treatment.

name: Imran v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a judicial review of a February 5, 2020 RPD decision (on court-ordered redetermination) denying the applicant's claim for refugee protection under sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA.
timing_evidence: The decision says only that the applicant decided to come to Canada after his September 2012 arrest and that a first refugee claim was denied in April 2014, without giving his date of first entry or the date the claim was made.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed.
basis_evidence: The claimant alleged he was targeted by religious extremists, the ISI and Pakistani authorities because of his human rights activism on behalf of Ahmadi, Christian and other religious minorities.

name: Hamid v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a judicial review of a RAD decision dated November 7, 2019 dismissing (on redetermination) the applicant's appeal from the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim.
timing_evidence: The applicant arrived in the U.S. on June 14, 2017, came to the Canadian border on July 1, 2017 and claimed refugee protection that day, his first entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed.
basis_evidence: The Chadian claimant alleged arrest, detention and torture by the National Security Agency arising from an ethnic conflict between his Gorane group and the Zaghawa and his mobilization of Gorane youth.

name: Tufino v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a judicial review of an RPD decision rejecting the applicant's claim for protection under the IRPA on state protection grounds.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no dates for the applicant's arrival in Canada or for when she made her refugee claim.
outcome_evidence: The RPD's decision was set aside and the matter referred back to a differently constituted panel for re-determination on directions.
basis_evidence: The claimant, a Mexican woman, alleged horrific sexual abuse at the hands of a man in a position of authority and police failure to protect women who have suffered relationship violence, with no SOGIE allegations.

name: Drammeh v. Canada (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a judicial review of an RPD decision dated October 10, 2017 finding the applicant not a Convention refugee, not a person in need of protection, and that his claim had no credible basis.
timing_evidence: The applicant travelled to Canada in May 2017 and made a refugee claim, with no indication of any earlier entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed, upholding the RPD's no credible basis finding.
basis_evidence: The minor claimant alleged risk of persecution in The Gambia because his father worked with the National Intelligence Agency of the former Jammeh regime, an imputed political/family-association claim.

name: Attalla v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a judicial review of an RPD decision dated May 1, 2018 refusing to reopen the applicants' refugee protection claims, which the RPD had declared abandoned before any merits hearing.
timing_evidence: Ms. Attalla and her children arrived at Pearson airport from Cairo on November 13, 2017 and she immediately told the CBSA she wanted to seek refugee protection, with no indication of any earlier entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was allowed, the RPD's refusal to reopen was set aside and the matter remitted for redetermination by a different decision-maker.
basis_evidence: Ms. Attalla claimed to fear persecution in Egypt for her opposition to the government and also claimed on behalf of her adult daughter Yasmeen that she was at risk because of her gender, with no SOGIE allegations.

name: Mbengani v.  Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is a PRRA officer's November 30, 2016 refusal of the applicant's pre-removal risk assessment application, not an RPD or RAD refugee determination (the earlier RPD/RAD refusals are only background).

name: Li v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a RAD decision dismissing Ms Li's appeal from the RPD's refusal of her refugee claim under ss. 96-97 of the IRPA.
timing_evidence: Ms Li first arrived in Canada on September 21, 2017 and claimed Convention refugee status 'several months later', i.e. within one year of entry.
outcome_evidence: The Court found no grounds to set aside the RAD's decision and the application for judicial review was dismissed.
basis_evidence: Ms Li alleged religious persecution in China as a Christian who attended an underground house church raided by the Public Security Bureau.

name: Amanuel v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a decision of a migration officer at the Canadian High Commission in Nairobi refusing an overseas application for permanent residence as a member of the refugee abroad class, not an RPD or RAD determination.

name: Lal v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a RAD decision confirming the RPD's finding that the applicants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection because of viable IFAs in India.
timing_evidence: The applicants left India for Canada on December 9, 2018 and made their claim for protection in June 2019, about six months after entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed, with the Court finding the RAD's IFA analysis reasonable.
basis_evidence: The applicants alleged persecution by the BJP and the Haryana police over an insufficient donation to the BJP and their perceived support for an opposing political party.

name: Nwokolo v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a RAD decision confirming the RPD's determination that the applicant is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1F(b) and is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: In 2019 the applicant fled Nigeria, travelled to the United States, then entered Canada and claimed refugee status upon entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed, the Court finding the RAD's exclusion decision reasonable and no breach of procedural fairness.
basis_evidence: The applicant, a pastor, alleged he was threatened and persecuted after refusing in 2018 to take a position as a chief priest, a religion-based claim.

name: Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v. Imeri
jr_refugee_evidence: The Ministers seek judicial review of an Immigration and Refugee Board (RPD) decision of October 2, 2008 accepting the respondent's claim for refugee protection and refusing to exclude him under Article 1F.
timing_evidence: The respondent's refugee claim was recorded in immigration officer port-of-entry notes dated June 8, 2003, indicating the claim was made at his entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The Ministers' application for judicial review was allowed and the Board's decision accepting the claim was set aside and referred back for rehearing, an unfavourable result for the claimant.
basis_evidence: The respondent, a Muslim Albanian minority activist in Macedonia who assisted the NLA, feared persecution by the Macedonian police for his political activities and ethnicity.

name: Damte v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a negative humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) decision under s. 25 of the IRPA, not an RPD or RAD refugee determination.

name: Kamel v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a Citizenship Officer's decision treating the applicant's citizenship application as abandoned under s. 13.2 of the Citizenship Act, not an RPD or RAD refugee determination.

name: Budai v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a Refugee Protection Division decision rejecting the Budai family's claim for refugee protection on state protection grounds.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no dates for the family's arrival in Canada or for when the refugee claim was made.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was allowed and the matter remitted to a differently constituted panel for re-determination.
basis_evidence: The applicants, Roma citizens of Hungary, alleged persecution by ethnic Hungarians, Neo Nazis and the police because of their Roma ethnicity.

name: Rahman v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a Refugee Protection Division decision of July 18, 2005 finding the applicants were not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicants all came to Canada from the United States in 2004 and claimed refugee status upon arrival that year, their first entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the Board's decision reasonable and the application for judicial review was dismissed.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged persecution based on membership in a particular social group (family) and religion arising from the interfaith marriage of a Bangladeshi Muslim man to a Mexican Christian woman.

name: Weekes v. Canada (Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a CBSA enforcement officer's decision refusing to defer the applicant's removal from Canada, not an RPD or RAD refugee determination.

name: Orozco v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the RPD's April 30, 2007 decision refusing to reopen Mr. Orozco's refugee protection claim, which had been denied by the RPD in October 2005.
timing_evidence: The decision says he lived and worked illegally in Miami for a number of years before entering Canada and applied for refugee protection on January 19, 2005, but gives no date for his first entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The Court found no reviewable error and ordered that 'The application for judicial review is dismissed.'
basis_evidence: His claim was based on being a gay man fearing persecution in Nicaragua at the hands of his father and other homophobic Nicaraguans.

name: Singh v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a RAD decision dismissing the appeal from the RPD's finding that the applicants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicants left India in December 2019 and made their claims for protection in August 2020, about eight months after arriving in Canada.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the RAD's IFA decision reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged harassment, detention and torture by Punjab police who suspected the family of harbouring the pro-Khalistani (SAD-A) brother-in-law and aiding Sikh militants (imputed political opinion).

name: Ettu v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a January 2023 RAD redetermination confirming that Mr. Ettu is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: Mr. Ettu came to Canada in July 2017 as a student, and the family sought refugee protection after his wife and children arrived in December 2018, more than one year after his first entry.
outcome_evidence: The Court held the RAD's decision was procedurally fair and reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged fear of the Supreme Eiye Confraternity cult, which harassed and threatened his wife because she had prosecuted a cult member for fraud.

name: Khan v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the RPD's October 21, 2004 decision dismissing the Khan family's claim for Convention refugee status and protection.
timing_evidence: The decision recites the 1994 killing in Pakistan and the 2004 RPD decision but gives no dates for Mr. Khan's entry to Canada or the making of his claim.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is allowed, the RPD decision is set aside and the application is remitted for redetermination before a differently constituted panel.
basis_evidence: Mr. Khan alleged fear of members of the MQM political party because he and his brother-in-law were the only witnesses to the MQM killing of a Shia doctor and two patients.

name: Tjuhanda v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the RPD's December 14, 2005 decision that the Tjuhanda family are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no dates for the applicants' entry to Canada or for the making of their refugee claim.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the Board's IFA conclusion not patently unreasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The applicants, Christians of Chinese descent from Indonesia (the principal applicant a Christian minister), claimed refugee status based on fear of persecution by Muslim extremists (religion/ethnicity).

name: Ibrahim v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the RAD's April 9, 2015 decision dismissing the appeal from the RPD's rejection of the applicant's refugee claim.
timing_evidence: The applicant arrived in Canada on November 11, 2013, and sought Canada's protection on November 27, 2013, about two weeks after entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is granted, the RAD's decision is set aside, and the matter returned to the RAD for redetermination by a different panel member.
basis_evidence: The applicant alleged Al-Shabaab attacked her Sufi minority-clan family, killed her father and brothers, and wanted to take her to become the wife of one of its members (forced marriage), a gender-based harm.

name: Cobani v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is a Senior Immigration Officer's January 17, 2025 refusal of the applicant's Pre-Removal Risk Assessment (PRRA) application, not an RPD or RAD determination.

name: Liang v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the RPD's May 1, 2019 redetermination decision that the applicant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicant came to Canada on November 22, 2012 and claimed protection shortly thereafter.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the RPD's credibility assessment reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim was based on the applicant's alleged practice of Falun Gong in China and fear of persecution by the Public Security Bureau (religion).

name: Nilani v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the RPD's June 11, 2003 decision that the applicant was not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no dates for the applicant's entry to Canada or for the making of her refugee claim.
outcome_evidence: The Court found no reviewable error and ordered that 'The application is dismissed.'
basis_evidence: The applicant, a Tamil citizen of Sri Lanka, claimed to fear persecution at the hands of the army, police, LTTE, and pro-government Tamil militant groups (ethnicity/imputed political opinion).

name: Godinez Ovalle v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a mandamus application under the Citizenship Act to compel the Minister to process the applicant's citizenship application, not a judicial review of an RPD or RAD refugee determination (the cessation application was still pending before the RPD).

name: Ogunrinde v. Canada (Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness)
jr_refugee_evidence: The application is for judicial review of a Senior Immigration Officer's decision refusing the Applicant's Pre-Removal Risk Assessment (PRRA), not an RPD or RAD refugee determination.

name: Selvarajah v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision dated February 6, 2013 refusing the Applicant's claim to be a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The Applicant arrived in Canada on August 13, 2010 aboard the MV Sun Sea as a refugee claimant and his claim proceeded from that arrival, so the claim was made within one year of first entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is allowed; the RPD Decision is quashed and the matter returned for reconsideration by a different Board member.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged risk from extortion and torture by the Karuna paramilitary group and perceived LTTE support as a Tamil MV Sun Sea passenger — political/ethnic/criminal grounds, not gender or SOGIE.

name: Souici v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a CIC officer's April 24, 2006 decision rejecting an application for permanent residence on humanitarian and compassionate grounds under s. 25 of IRPA, not an RPD/RAD refugee determination.

name: Agazuma v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the December 18, 2019 RAD decision dismissing the Applicants' appeal from the RPD's refusal of their refugee claims.
timing_evidence: The Applicants arrived in the US on March 27, 2018, came to Canada three days later and claimed refugee protection immediately, so the claim was made well within one year of first entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is dismissed, leaving the RAD's rejection of the claims in place.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged threats by family elders who wanted the Principal Applicant's daughters to undergo female genital mutilation, a gender-based form of persecution.

name: Lowell v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the refusal of an H&C application for permanent residence from within Canada (decided by a PRRA officer), not an RPD/RAD refugee determination.

name: Marita v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the RPD's June 18, 2019 decision dismissing the refugee claims of Ms. Marita and her daughter under the Article 1F(b) exclusion.
timing_evidence: Ms. Marita first entered Canada on November 7, 2008 on a visitor visa and only made her refugee claim at a CBSA interview on February 3, 2011, more than one year after first entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is granted and the matter remitted to the RPD for redetermination by another member.
basis_evidence: She alleged that after refusing her adoptive father's demand that she become his third wife he harassed, threatened and assaulted her and attempted to kidnap her daughter — gender-based persecution (forced marriage/related violence).

name: Yoon v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision rejecting the Applicant's gender-based refugee protection claim.
timing_evidence: The Applicant arrived in Canada on December 24, 2007 and made her refugee claim on April 29, 2008, about four months after entry.
outcome_evidence: The Court set the RPD's decision aside and referred the matter back to a differently constituted panel for re-determination.
basis_evidence: The claim was a gender-based claim founded on years of extreme physical, sexual and mental abuse by her husband (domestic violence).

name: Liu v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a RAD decision dated January 26, 2022 confirming the RPD's finding that the Applicant was not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The decision recites no dates of the Applicant's entry to Canada or of when his refugee claim was made, so the gap cannot be determined.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is dismissed.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged a fear of persecution in China as a Falun Gong practitioner, a religion/spiritual-practice-based claim.

name: Osoble v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the RPD's May 31, 2022 decision vacating the Applicant's Convention refugee status under section 109 of IRPA.
timing_evidence: The Applicant entered Canada in April 2017 (April 8 on his account, April 15 on the Minister's) and the RPD granted his refugee claim on February 21, 2018, so the claim was necessarily made less than one year after first entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is dismissed, leaving the vacation of the Applicant's refugee status in place.
basis_evidence: The decision addresses only identity/nationality misrepresentation and never describes the persecution alleged in the underlying Somali refugee claim.

name: Ballatore v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of the RPD's May 31, 2004 decision finding the applicants were neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The decision states the principal applicant filed her refugee claim five months after arriving in Canada on a visitor's visa.
outcome_evidence: The Court dismissed the application for judicial review, upholding the RPD's negative credibility decision.
basis_evidence: The principal applicant alleged persecution as a woman victim of domestic violence at the hands of her husband, who also allegedly terrorized her sons.

name: Adeniji-Adele v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a RAD decision finding the applicants neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection due to IFAs in Port Harcourt and Abuja.
timing_evidence: Principal claimant Agnes first entered Canada on August 30, 2015 accompanying her daughter, and the claim was made after she returned with her son on June 7, 2017, more than one year after first entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is dismissed.
basis_evidence: The applicants alleged the estate Executor demanded that the daughter return to Nigeria, marry his friend's son, and renounce Christianity for Islam — a forced marriage (gender-based) allegation with no SOGIE component.

name: Singh c. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a July 16, 2014 Refugee Protection Division decision rejecting the applicant's refugee claim.
timing_evidence: The RPD found he 'waited too long to claim refugee status' but the decision gives no entry date or claim date from which a gap can be computed.
outcome_evidence: The application is allowed; the RPD decision is set aside and the matter returned to another decision-maker for procedural fairness breaches.
basis_evidence: The decision refers only to a non-credible 'persecution narrative' without describing the type of persecution alleged.

name: Avila Magana v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a September 25, 2020 RAD decision confirming the rejection of the applicant's refugee protection claim.
timing_evidence: The applicant arrived in Canada in November 2018 but the decision does not state when the refugee claim was made, so the gap cannot be computed.
outcome_evidence: The Court dismisses the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim was based on fear of PRI militants in Mexico because of the applicant's political involvement with a rival party (political opinion).

name: Jirrow v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is a Senior Immigration Officer's refusal of an H&C permanent residence application, not an RPD/RAD refugee determination (the earlier RPD/RAD decisions are only mentioned as background).

name: Mabadi v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an April 28, 2014 RPD decision finding the applicant neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The decision says the applicant was in Canada in 2012 when her family was attacked but gives no date of first entry to Canada and no date the refugee claim was made.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is dismissed; the interpretation was found adequate and the hearing fair.
basis_evidence: The applicant alleged the DRC government targeted her because of her participation in anti-government marches (political opinion), with state agents attacking her family in retaliation.

name: Singh v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a March 7, 2003 Refugee Protection Division decision concluding the applicant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicant fled India and arrived in Canada on June 18, 2002 and made his refugee claim on June 20, 2002, two days after entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is allowed and the matter submitted to a differently constituted panel for reconsideration.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged persecution of a young Sikh by Punjab police due to his Sikh religion and his family's suspected connections to militants (religion/imputed political opinion).

name: Hossain v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is an IRCC officer's April 13, 2021 refusal of a Pre-Removal Risk Assessment (PRRA) application; the applicant was ineligible for referral to the RPD.

name: Twebaze v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The underlying proceeding is an application for leave and judicial review of a May 11, 2011 Refugee Protection Division decision denying the applicant's claim for protection; this ruling is a Rule 397 reconsideration motion in that proceeding.
timing_evidence: The decision contains no facts about when the applicant entered Canada or when her refugee claim was made.
outcome_evidence: The application for leave and judicial review was dismissed for failure to file a record, and the Court dismisses the motion to reconsider that dismissal, leaving the claimant unsuccessful.
basis_evidence: The decision describes only procedural matters and says nothing about the type of persecution alleged in the underlying claim.

name: Shah v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a June 28, 2012 Refugee Protection Division decision finding the applicant neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicant 'came to Canada in 2010, claiming protection', a reasonable inference that the claim was made upon or shortly after his arrival, within one year of first entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is dismissed; the Board's global adverse credibility finding was reasonable.
basis_evidence: The applicant, a Pakistani businessman, alleged fear of the Taliban who he claimed extorted, shot and attacked him (criminal/militant extortion, not gender- or SOGIE-based).

name: Kibiku v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a January 23, 2024 RAD redetermination decision confirming the RPD's rejection of the applicant's refugee protection claim.
timing_evidence: The applicant fled Kenya and arrived in Canada on September 9, 2019, 'submitting a claim for refugee protection soon thereafter'.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review is dismissed as the applicant did not establish a reviewable error in the RAD's credibility findings.
basis_evidence: The applicant alleged risk from his half-uncles and the criminal Mungiki group arising from a family land dispute in Kenya (not gender- or SOGIE-based).

name: Lin v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a June 28, 2016 RAD decision confirming the RPD's determination that the applicants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicants arrived in Canada on tourist visas on October 2, 2015, and their claim had already been heard by the RPD and decided by the RAD by June 28, 2016, so the claim was made less than a year after entry.
outcome_evidence: THIS COURT'S JUDGMENT is that this application for judicial review is dismissed.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged risk under China's family planning regime, including the forced abortion already inflicted on Ms. Lin, mandatory IUD use and pregnancy checkups, and threatened sterilization -- gender-specific reproductive coercion.

name: Fermin Mora v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a September 28, 2017 RAD decision confirming the RPD's finding that the applicant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicant arrived in Canada in May 2014 but did not file her claim for refugee protection until February 2, 2016, a wait of nearly 21 months.
outcome_evidence: THIS COURT'S JUDGMENT is that the application for judicial review is dismissed.
basis_evidence: The applicant alleged she feared for her life and mistreatment by her jealous ex-husband, who threatened to kill her with a machete -- intimate-partner/domestic violence.

name: Omokri v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a September 1, 2017 RAD decision refusing to re-open the applicant's appeal of the RPD's dismissal of her refugee claim, part of the RPD/RAD refugee determination process.
timing_evidence: The applicant entered Canada on January 3, 2016 and sought protection as a Convention refugee, with the RPD deciding the claim by January 24, 2017, indicating the claim was made within a year of entry.
outcome_evidence: THIS COURT'S JUDGMENT is that the application for judicial review is dismissed.
basis_evidence: She sought protection on the basis of risk to her life arising from her status as a bisexual woman -- a SOGIE-based claim.

name: Togtokh v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is a Senior Immigration Officer's July 21, 2017 rejection of the applicant's pre-removal risk assessment (PRRA) application, not an RPD or RAD refugee determination.

name: Kule v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review seeking to quash the July 18, 2005 RPD decision rejecting the applicant's refugee claim under sections 96 and 97 of IRPA.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no date of the applicant's entry to Canada and no date on which the refugee claim was made, so the gap cannot be computed.
outcome_evidence: The judicial review application is allowed, the tribunal's decision is set aside and the claims are remitted to the Board for re-consideration by a differently constituted tribunal.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged persecution by Socialist Party supporters and mafia-linked extortionists targeting his father, based on perceived political opinion and membership in an anti-Communist family.

name: Firooznam v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a March 4, 2022 RAD decision dismissing the applicant's appeal and confirming the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim under Article 1F(a) exclusion.
timing_evidence: The applicant fled Iran for Canada in September 2018 but the decision does not state when he made his refugee claim, so the gap between first entry and claim cannot be determined.
outcome_evidence: THIS COURT'S JUDGMENT is that the application for judicial review is dismissed.
basis_evidence: The applicant alleged a fear of being tortured and killed by the Iranian authorities because he believes he is wanted for espionage after leaking confidential information and interfering with regime security systems -- imputed political opinion.

name: Rodriguez v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a July 20, 2021 RAD decision dismissing the applicants' appeal of the RPD's rejection of their refugee claims.
timing_evidence: The decision recounts a June 2017 robbery in Colombia and a November 23, 2020 RPD hearing but never states when the applicants entered Canada or when they made their claim.
outcome_evidence: THIS COURT'S JUDGMENT is that the application for judicial review is dismissed.
basis_evidence: The family alleged fear of persecution or harm at the hands of an armed criminal group that robbed the family's restaurant in Colombia and threatened them -- criminality with no gender or SOGIE component.

name: Sarker v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a June 2, 2004 decision of the Immigration and Refugee Board, Refugee Protection Division, determining the applicant was not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no date of the applicant's entry to Canada and no date on which his refugee claim was made.
outcome_evidence: THIS COURT ORDERS THAT: The application for judicial review is dismissed.
basis_evidence: The applicant claimed a well-founded fear of persecution by the police and members of the rival Awami League by reason of his political activities as a member of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party.

name: Prekaj v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a January 19, 2009 RPD decision refusing the applicants' application to be deemed Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicants fled from the United States to Canada specifically to seek refugee status after their US asylum claim was denied, supporting the inference that the claim was made on or shortly after their first entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The application is allowed. The Decision is quashed and the matter is returned for reconsideration by a different officer.
basis_evidence: The applicants feared returning to Albania because of a blood feud in the male applicant's family, with the victim's family seeking to kill a male member of his family.

name: Rajanayagam v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decisions under review are negative Pre-Removal Risk Assessment (PRRA) and humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) decisions, not RPD or RAD refugee determinations (the 2007 RPD refusal is only background).

name: Islam v. Canada (Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is an Immigration Division determination of January 9, 2019 that the applicant is inadmissible on security grounds under paragraphs 34(1)(f) and 34(1)(c) IRPA for BNP membership, not an RPD or RAD refugee determination.

name: Jiang v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is a CIC officer's December 8, 2011 refusal of an H&C application for permanent residence from within Canada, not an RPD or RAD refugee determination.

name: Tung v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision of February 27, 2018 granting the Minister's application for cessation of the applicant's refugee protection under paragraphs 108(1)(a) and 108(1)(e) IRPA.
timing_evidence: The decision states only that the applicant was granted refugee status in Canada in 2002 and gives no date of her first entry to Canada or of when her claim was made.
outcome_evidence: The Court held that 'this judicial review is dismissed', leaving the RPD's cessation of the applicant's refugee status intact.
basis_evidence: The underlying refugee claim was based on fear of persecution in China as a Falun Gong practitioner, a religious/political ground rather than gender or SOGIE.

name: Molnar v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a negative decision of the Refugee Protection Division of the Immigration and Refugee Board rendered October 31, 2002 rejecting the applicant's refugee claim.
timing_evidence: The applicant left Liberia for Edmonton on August 17, 2001 and claimed refugee status there on August 20, 2001, three days after arriving in Canada.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was allowed and the matter returned to the Board for re-consideration before a differently constituted panel.
basis_evidence: The applicant alleged a well-founded fear of persecution as a member of a particular social group of females fearing female genital mutilation, which her mother planned to have performed on her through the Sande secret society.

name: Aghdaragh v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision dated April 13, 2007 finding the applicant to be neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: After fleeing Iran via the Netherlands, Germany, St. Martine and Trinidad, the decision states that 'Upon arrival in Canada, the applicant made his claim for refugee status,' i.e. the claim was made at his first entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was allowed and the matter referred back to a newly constituted panel of the Board for redetermination.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged persecution by the Iranian regime (political opinion) for exposing corruption at Iran Khodro through flyers, washroom writings and encouraging strikes, with agents raiding his family home.

name: Ortiz Garcia v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a Refugee Protection Division decision determining that the applicant is not a person in need of protection under section 97 and rejecting her claim for refugee protection on credibility grounds.
timing_evidence: The applicant and her children left Mexico for Canada on September 19, 2007 and she claimed refugee protection that same day, with no indication of any earlier entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The Court dismissed the application for judicial review, upholding the Board's rejection of her claim.
basis_evidence: The applicant alleged threats and a sexual assault on June 19, 2007 by two men sent by her spouse's former employee, and the Court analyzed the Board's application of the Guidelines on Women Refugee Claimants Fearing Gender-Related Persecution.

name: Machedon v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision dated April 22, 2003 determining that the applicants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicants arrived in Halifax, Nova Scotia on June 7, 2001 and claimed refugee status four days later.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was allowed, the Board's decision quashed and the claims remitted back to the Board for redetermination.
basis_evidence: The husband-and-wife claimants alleged persecution in Romania on the basis of their Roma ethnicity, including beatings, detention, extortion and discrimination.

name: Canada (Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness) v. Zinali
jr_refugee_evidence: The Minister seeks judicial review of an RPD decision rejecting an application to cease the respondent's refugee protection under section 108(1)(a) IRPA.
timing_evidence: The respondent was granted overseas refugee protection by a visa officer in Turkey before arriving in Canada in October 2013, so her refugee claim clearly was not made more than one year after her first entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The Minister's application for judicial review was dismissed, so the RPD's refusal to cease the claimant's refugee protection stands and she keeps her status.
basis_evidence: The respondent fled Iran because she feared persecution as an adherent of the Baha'i religion.

name: Ulaganathan v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a May 25, 2023 RAD decision dismissing the applicant's appeal of an RPD decision finding him neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: Upon his release from a four-day police detention following his March 21, 2018 arrest, the applicant 'fled the country seeking refugee status in Canada,' indicating the claim was made upon arrival with no mention of any earlier entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The Court's judgment is that 'The application for judicial review is dismissed,' upholding the RAD's rejection of the claim on IFA grounds.
basis_evidence: The applicant, a farmer of the Ambalakarar caste, alleged persecution in India by upper-caste landlords and complicit local police because he employed Dalit workers, a caste/social-group claim unrelated to gender or SOGIE.

name: Chen v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision determining the applicant was neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection, based on disbelief that she was a Falun Gong member wanted by the PSB.
timing_evidence: The applicant left China on October 29, 2011, arrived in Canada on November 5, 2011, and claimed refugee protection three days later.
outcome_evidence: The application was allowed, the RPD decision set aside, and the claim sent to a differently constituted panel for determination.
basis_evidence: The applicant alleged fear of persecution in China as a practitioner of the banned Falun Gong movement after the PSB raided her underground practice group and sought her arrest.

name: Feyissa v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a September 3, 2021 RAD decision dismissing the applicant's appeal and upholding the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim.
timing_evidence: The applicant entered Canada on July 21, 2019 and claimed refugee protection, with no earlier entry to Canada mentioned.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the RAD decision reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged racial discrimination amounting to persecution against an Ethiopian man of Amhara ethnicity in Germany (employment and healthcare discrimination).

name: Rukoro v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a May 9, 2019 RPD decision denying the applicants' refugee and person in need of protection claims.
timing_evidence: The applicants arrived in Canada from Namibia in 2011 and submitted their refugee claims shortly after their arrival.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed, upholding the RPD's rejection of the claims.
basis_evidence: The principal claimant alleged persecution as a bisexual man (SOGIE) while his partner alleged fear of being forced into prostitution by her aunt, argued as gender-based persecution under the Gender Guidelines.

name: Lopez Escobedo v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a RAD decision confirming the RPD's rejection of the applicants' refugee claims on IFA grounds.
timing_evidence: The decision recites no dates for the applicants' entry to Canada or the making of their refugee claims.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was allowed, the RAD decision set aside, and the matter remitted to a differently constituted RAD panel for redetermination.
basis_evidence: The applicants claimed protection based on their fear of persecution from the Los Zetas cartel in Mexico, which sought a monthly quota from them.

name: Rosas Maldonado v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision finding the applicants were neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicants obtained passports and traveled to Montreal where they claimed refugee status, indicating the claim was made upon arrival, with no earlier entry to Canada mentioned.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed, the Board's IFA finding being reasonable.
basis_evidence: The daughter alleged kidnapping, sexual assault, and a forced abortion attempt by her violent boyfriend after she became pregnant, with the applicants arguing gender-related persecution under the Gender Guidelines.

name: Liu v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is a senior immigration officer's refusal of a humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) application for permanent residence under s. 25(1) of the IRPA, not an RPD/RAD refugee determination.

name: Puri v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is an immigration officer's May 17, 2017 refusal of an application for permanent residence on humanitarian and compassionate grounds under s. 25(1) of the IRPA, not an RPD/RAD refugee determination.

name: Hammed v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a January 17, 2006 RPD decision rejecting the applicant's refugee protection claim.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no dates for the applicant's entry to Canada or the making of her refugee claim.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed, the IFA and identity findings standing despite concerns about the credibility analysis.
basis_evidence: The applicant based her claim on fear of her uncle who allegedly sexually abused her for years and threatened to kill her, with the Court referencing the Board's Gender Guidelines.

name: Sernas De Toro v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a July 19, 2011 RPD determination that the applicants were not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicants fled Colombia to Canada after a July 21, 2009 threatening call and claimed refugee protection on September 25, 2009, with no earlier entry to Canada mentioned.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was dismissed, the state protection and IFA findings being reasonable.
basis_evidence: The claim was based on fear of the FARC, which extorted and threatened the applicants after the killing of the principal applicant's husband.

name: Gurusamy v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a RAD decision dismissing the applicant's refugee claim by confirming the RPD's Article 1E/s. 98 exclusion finding based on his Italian permanent resident status.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no dates for the applicant's entry to Canada or the making of his refugee claim.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was granted and the matter remitted for redetermination.
basis_evidence: The applicant, a Christian Tamil from Colombo, alleged fear of persecution in Sri Lanka, indicating ethnic/religious grounds with no gender-based or SOGIE allegations.

name: Nunaj v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is an Immigration Appeal Division decision dismissing an appeal from the refusal of a family-class parental sponsorship application for failure to meet minimum necessary income requirements, not an RPD/RAD refugee determination.

name: Devilmé v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a motion to stay a removal order incidental to a judicial review of a December 2, 2011 removal order issued under subsection 44(2) of IRPA, and the Court notes the applicant did not seek judicial review of the RPD or PRRA decisions.

name: Singh v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Mr. Singh seeks judicial review of a Refugee Appeal Division decision dismissing his claim for asylum on the basis of an internal flight alternative.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no date of the applicant's entry to Canada or of the making of his refugee claim, so the gap cannot be computed.
outcome_evidence: The Court held the RAD's IFA finding was reasonable and the application for judicial review is dismissed.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged detention and torture by the Punjab police who suspected him of harbouring and helping Sikh militants, an imputed political/militancy-related claim with no gender or SOGIE allegations.

name: Negash v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The applicant seeks judicial review of the January 13, 2012 decision of the Refugee Protection Division finding he was neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicant arrived in Canada in October 2010 and made a claim for refugee protection in December 2010, about two months after entry.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the Board's identity and credibility findings reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged religious persecution in Eritrea based on the applicant's membership in the Pentecostal Church, including arrest and beating during a raid on a Pentecostal gathering.

name: Velez v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is an application for judicial review of a Refugee Protection Division decision determining the applicant was neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicant left Colombia for Canada on October 2, 2007 and applied for refugee status in early January 2008, roughly three months after arrival.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the Board's internal flight alternative finding in Bogota reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged fear of the FARC, who demanded use of his employer's trucks and threatened him, a criminal/guerrilla-based claim with no gender or SOGIE allegations.

name: Budai v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Ms. Budai seeks judicial review of a Refugee Appeal Division decision dismissing her appeal from the RPD's refusal of her refugee claim.
timing_evidence: Ms. Budai left Hungary for Canada in November 2017 to claim refugee protection and the RPD denied the claim in March 2018, so the claim was made well within a year of first entry.
outcome_evidence: The Court held Ms. Budai had not established that the RAD's decision was unreasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged persecution based on Roma ethnicity but also included allegations of domestic violence by her abusive father and she advanced her profile as a young single woman abused by her father, with no SOGIE allegations.

name: Singh v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is an application for judicial review of a November 16, 2005 Refugee Protection Division decision that the applicant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicant arrived in Canada on September 24, 2003 and filed his refugee claim in Montreal on March 18, 2005, a delay of almost eighteen months.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the RPD's credibility decision reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review, relying in part on the delay in claiming.
basis_evidence: The Sikh priest applicant alleged harassment, illegal detention and torture by Indian police over his suspected association with Sikh militants, a religious/imputed political claim with no gender or SOGIE allegations.

name: Singh v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is an application for judicial review of a September 17, 2024 Refugee Appeal Division decision upholding the RPD's finding that the applicant was neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The decision states the applicant left India for Canada in January 2023 but gives no date on which the refugee claim was made, so the gap cannot be computed.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the RAD's credibility analysis reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged fear of Hindu fundamentalist groups, the BJP and police due to the applicant's conversion to Christianity, his Scheduled Caste background and his support of the AAP, with no gender or SOGIE allegations.

name: Jayasinghe Arachchige v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is an application for judicial review of the March 5, 2019 Refugee Appeal Division decision dismissing the applicant's appeal from the RPD's denial of his refugee claim.
timing_evidence: The applicant remained in the USA until 2017 and then entered Canada and made a refugee claim, indicating the claim was made upon or shortly after his first entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The Court found no reviewable error in the RAD's decision and the application for judicial review is dismissed.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged persecution by Sri Lankan government officials and presidential security agents who beat and threatened him and accused him of LTTE associations, a political claim with no gender or SOGIE allegations.

name: Alexander v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: The decision under review is a Senior Immigration Officer's November 5, 2019 rejection of a pre-removal risk assessment (PRRA) application, not an RPD or RAD refugee determination.

name: Wilson v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is an application for judicial review of an October 2, 2014 Refugee Protection Division decision determining the applicant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicant arrived in Canada on April 17, 2012 and claimed refugee protection shortly thereafter.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the RPD's findings on delay and state protection reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim was based on the applicant's fear of the man who assaulted and raped her in St. Vincent and the Grenadines and threatened to kill her if she went to the police, a gender-based sexual violence claim with no SOGIE allegations.

name: Karas v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a RAD decision dated September 16, 2020 dismissing the applicant's appeal and rejecting his refugee protection claim.
timing_evidence: The applicant arrived in Canada on August 18, 2014 and claimed refugee protection on December 3, 2014, well within one year of entry.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the RAD's IFA finding reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The claim was based on extortion, threats and assaults by the Yumaks criminal gang in Ukraine, aided by corrupt police.

name: Cisse v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of a RAD decision dated October 25, 2021 rejecting the applicant's refugee protection claim on credibility grounds.
timing_evidence: The decision gives no date of the applicant's entry to Canada or of when the refugee claim was made, so the gap cannot be determined.
outcome_evidence: The Court found the RAD's credibility assessment reasonable and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: The underlying claim involved political persecution in Guinea connected to a May 28, 2019 demonstration, an arrest warrant, and a letter from the Union des Forces Democratiques de Guinee.

name: Pereira Dos Santos v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision dated May 30, 2011 determining the applicant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The applicant entered Canada as a visitor in 2004 and submitted her refugee claim on February 6, 2009, more than one year after first entry.
outcome_evidence: The Court found no reviewable error in the RPD's state protection analysis and dismissed the application for judicial review.
basis_evidence: She alleged fear of her former boyfriend, the father of her child, in a claim the Board assessed as gender-related violence against women in Brazil.

name: Cuni v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision refusing to reinstate the applicants' withdrawn refugee protection claim, a decision of the Refugee Protection Division in their refugee claim.
timing_evidence: Ms. Cuni and her son arrived in Canada on June 28, 2008 and filed their refugee claim upon arrival that same day.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was granted and the matter referred back to another decision maker for re-determination and re-instatement of the claim.
basis_evidence: The decision only states the family came from Kosovo and that the merits of the claim were never tested; the type of persecution alleged is not described.

name: Abbass v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision dated March 23, 2021 rejecting the applicant's claim for refugee protection under sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA.
timing_evidence: The applicant flew from Lebanon to New York on September 18, 2018 and claimed refugee protection at the Fort Erie port of entry on September 20, 2018, his first entry to Canada.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was allowed, the RPD decision set aside, and the matter remitted for redetermination by a different decision maker.
basis_evidence: The claim alleged persecution of the applicant as a stateless Palestinian in Lebanon through cumulative discrimination, inability to return, work and property restrictions, and risks from armed factions in the Ain al-Hilweh camp.

name: Nagy v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: This is a judicial review of a Senior Immigration Officer's decision dismissing a pre-removal risk assessment (PRRA) application, not an RPD or RAD refugee determination.

name: Yoon v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
jr_refugee_evidence: Judicial review of an RPD decision dated June 13, 2011 determining the applicants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection.
timing_evidence: The principal applicant Sechan Yoon arrived in Canada on July 30, 2009 and claimed refugee protection on August 5, 2009, within days of entry.
outcome_evidence: The application for judicial review was allowed and the case remitted for reconsideration by a differently constituted panel due to interpretation errors at the hearing.
basis_evidence: The family alleged fear of JMS sect leaders as traitors for leaving the sect, including that the wife was sexually assaulted by sect religious leaders and feared her daughter would suffer the same sexual violence; no SOGIE allegations.

name: Zeballos v. Canada (Citizenship and Immigration)
